nodes.question: How does the study intend to apply the MCA methodology?
nodes.answer: The study intends to apply the MCA methodology at in-person or online workshops through a tool for identifying and prioritizing NBS/BES.
nodes.paragraph: Maleki et al. (2018) [ 28] apply Multicriteria-Spatial Decision Support System (MSDSS) for prioritization of wetland restoration using different scenarios. MCA has also been used for area prioritization through ranking of criteria. Valente et al. (2021) [29] used a mixed method of participatory analysis and multi-criteria evaluation to identify priority areas for forest restoration coupled with water related ecosystem services. The typical structure of MCA includes the identification of the relevant criteria and alter - natives from the existing theory and practice, the assignment of numerical values to criteria to indicate their relative importance and to quantify the impacts of the alternatives on these criteria, and the use of a formal mathematical procedure for analyzing numerical values to determine the ranking (priorities) of the alternatives [ 30]. The objective of this study is to present the development of a participatory and replicable MCA methodology and its application at in-person or online workshops, through a tool for identifying and prioritizing NBS/BES that cover the WEFE nexus and have a considerable impact on socio-economic parameters [ 2, 4].
